Blender is awesome and has an amazing MCP but it’s not well suited for CAD design. It uses polygonal meshes.

A better way to do CAD modelling is via mathematical B-Rep solids via OpenCASCADE kernel using CadQuery

I made a skill that provides tools to do precision modelling directly in Claude or Codex app
what_they_built: A skill that gives Claude or Codex precision CAD tools built on CadQuery and OpenCASCADE B-Rep solids, instead of Blender’s polygon meshes.

text:
here's how i built this character animation concept with fable 5.2...

one red panda courier, one goal: reach the flag on the other side of the gap.

the challenge was making 10 seconds feel like a real story beat while keeping the character consistent: same scarf, same scrolls, same fur on every frame.

step 1: design the character first. teal scarf, worn jacket, backpack scrolls, fluffy striped tail. every detail has to survive the movement.

step 2: block out the scene. a plain white platform and a golden flag as the goal, so the eye always knows where the action is going.

step 3: plan the action in short beats: stand and study the goal, crouch, launch, glide through the air, land.

step 4: animate from the first frame with the camera mostly fixed, so any problem with the pose or the tail is easy to spot.

step 5: check every transition for sliding feet, changing proportions, flickering fur and clipping scrolls.

step 6: finish with a close-up. the determined face before the jump sells the whole moment.

what made the setup better was planning the transitions. the look at the flag leads into the crouch. the crouch leads into the jump. every beat gives the next one somewhere to start.

this is a generated animation concept, not a production-ready game rig.

save this for your next character animation test
what_they_built: A 10-second character animation concept of a red panda courier crossing a gap to reach a flag, with the same scarf, scrolls and fur kept consistent in every frame, with the steps shared in the thread.

text:
Got so many AI chats going your brain might explode? Which one's stuck waiting on you? Which one finished 20 minutes ago and is just… sitting there, politely?

So I built a free VS Code extension that rounds them all up. Hope it helps you!

What is it?

Every Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity chat, across every window, in one tidy list. A spinner while it works, a little yellow bell when it needs you, a green tick when it's done. Plus how much of your plan is left before the rate limit pulls the plug and you cry.

Click a chat and you're there, even if it lives in another window. No more dropdown digging. No more window roulette. Honestly can't work without it now.

Setup takes a minute:
https://github.com/ubrandon/ai-status
